name: Paspalum
common_group: Paspalums — six existing Hays County Botany learner species

project_scope.selection_mode: existing manifest species FINISH/ENRICH (no new first-card admission)
project_scope.taxonomic_review: Species-level identity and native-by-county audit remain as they were; this is a structural visual learner pass, not new verification.

look_here_first: PASPALUM: start with ONE complete flowering head, count the one-sided racemes and inspect flat oval spikelets in rows. Then check the rooted base (wet stolon mat or perennial tuft) and five measured ripe spikelets for glume size/hairs. Branch count overlaps, so two racemes alone do not prove knotgrass, and many racemes alone do not prove vaseygrass.
shared_morphology: Paspalum usually has one or more unilateral, spike-like reproductive RACEMES; each raceme is a branch of the full inflorescence.
Green oval compressed units seen on these racemes are SPIKELETS, each with distinct glumes/sterile and fertile florets; purple flower parts may protrude during anthesis.
A grass leaf consists of blade, basal sheath and a ligule at their junction. Correct collar photography requires blade/sheath movement rather than a distant tuft photo.
A mature measured spikelet macro plus habitat/growth habit and a complete raceme count is often required for species-level separation.

study_strategy.priority: Photo-led field recognition first, reproductive anatomy second
crew_sequence: 1. Photograph one entire flowering stem and count attached unilateral racemes; do not count overlapping stems.
2. Learn original head photos plus added Florida paspalum seedhead, thin paspalum full-raceme, and knotgrass low mat.
3. On DALLIS vs VASEY measure 5 mature spikelets: roughly 3–4 vs 2–3 mm, respectively; both can have long marginal hairs, and raceme counts overlap.
4. For FLORIDA vs PUBIFLORUM compare true large rounded vs smaller oval spikelets and upper-glume details, not tuft height.
5. For KNOTGRASS vs THIN PASPALUM locate a genuine rooting stolon and leaf blade/collar hairs; V-shaped heads do not prove knotgrass.
6. Photograph blade-sheath collar, rooted base, ripe glume and mm scale from the same plant; preserve existing nativity status.

six_species_field_key.field_hint: Usually V-shaped two-raceme head PLUS an actually rooted aboveground stolon; new Aussie mat photograph illustrates low habit only.
six_species_field_key.next_check: Photo of ROOTED node, same-plant full seedhead and mature spikelets to exclude P. notatum.

six_species_field_key.field_hint: One/few slim one-sided flowering racemes; new full raceme/leaf view complements prior spikelet macro. Purple projections are flowers, not seeds.
six_species_field_key.next_check: Check true blade/sheath hairs, collar, mature glumes and variety—not diagnosable from two flowering photos alone.

six_species_field_key.field_hint: Usually several racemes with tight oval flattened spikelet pairs about 2.7–3.2 mm in references
six_species_field_key.next_check: Upper-glume fine hairs, spikelet size, full raceme count and collar; source photo only shows one fragment

six_species_field_key.field_hint: Large perennial tuft with usually a FEW flowering racemes. Newly available licensed real photo shows a 3-branched head with rounded attached spikelets.
six_species_field_key.next_check: True mature 3.5–5 mm spikelets with a 1-mm ruler and glumes; garden photo is not a Hays voucher.

six_species_field_key.field_hint: Coarse dallisgrass, generally several (often 3–7) racemes, hairy larger about 3–4 mm spikelets
six_species_field_key.next_check: Measure multiple mature silky-margined spikelets; compare entire head with vaseygrass

six_species_field_key.field_hint: Tall coarse introduced vaseygrass, generally MANY (commonly 10–20) slender racemes on elongated axis
six_species_field_key.next_check: Measure smaller roughly 2–3 mm edge-hairy spikelets, check true basal plant and collar; count overlaps

six_species_field_key.field_hint: Head fragment, overlap, juvenile flowering stage or missing collar/mature spikelets
six_species_field_key.next_check: Label Paspalum sp. pending properly documented flowering mature specimens

comparison_cards.title: Dallisgrass versus vaseygrass
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Count racemes attached to the WHOLE head and examine measured marginally hairy spikelets.

field_matrix.dilatatum: Coarse clumping grass, often around 1 m
field_matrix.urvillei: Usually taller robust grass, often 1–2.5 m

field_matrix.dilatatum: Larger around 3–4 mm with conspicuous long silky margin hairs
field_matrix.urvillei: Smaller around 2–3 mm with hairs at margin

comparison_cards.stop_rule: Don't classify without a complete head and several measured spikelets; height and branch counts overlap.

comparison_cards.title: Knotgrass versus thin paspalum
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Trace actual creeping stolon nodes and check full flowering head/leaf hairiness.

field_matrix.setaceum: More variable leafy growth with varieties needing foliage inspection

field_matrix.distichum: Typically two terminal V-shaped unilateral racemes
field_matrix.setaceum: Often one to a few unilateral branches; can look close
Leaf hairs, measured small spikelets, collar

comparison_cards.stop_rule: Additional knotgrass wet-meadow habit and thin paspalum full-raceme photos available. Neither shows the required actual rooted stolon or variety-level leaf pubescence. Two racemes also occur in P. notatum.

comparison_cards.title: Florida paspalum versus pubiflorum
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Measure mature spikelets and show the COMPLETE head, don't just compare plant size.

field_matrix.clue: Often large coarser upright clump and larger rounded mature spikelets
Several racemes and smaller roughly 2.7–3.2 mm oval spikelets, glumes variable pubescence

comparison_cards.stop_rule: Florida paspalum now has real source-labelled flowering racemes as well as tuft, but NO measured glume macro. Pubiflorum still lacks full head and glume hair detail. No definitive species call from imagery alone.

visual_comparison.title: Paspalum — 6 installed species, 10 real credited photo panels
visual_comparison.subtitle: Seven preserved archived panels plus three independently licensed external references, awaiting user photo review; new arrows target visible structures only. Four additional genuinely original Bob Harms P. pubiflorum photos now physically stored, shared by species and genus, original creator and copyright preserved, not CC.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: WHOLE HEAD → RACEME COUNT → 1-mm RIPE SPIKELET → EDGE HAIRS → ROOTED BASE + COLLAR.

items.label: FLORIDA PASPALUM — actual flowering racemes
items.image_role: Separate real flowering-head photograph from US Botanic Garden: three one-sided spikelet-bearing racemes on one stem, not a Texas wild voucher
items.caption: David J. Stang photographed a flowering Florida paspalum with three divergent racemes and clearly visible rounded green attached spikelets. Unlike the original plant-habit photo, this actually shows the inflorescence. There is no millimeter scale, collar or dissected glume: do not claim 3.5–5 mm spikelet measurements from these pixels.
items.why_it_matters: Closes the missing seedhead shape in the original Florida paspalum learner. Compare the few branches and large-looking rounded spikelets with pubiflorum and dallisgrass, then measure a real specimen.
